clue.text: Consternation is hell for T

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so his name stands for hell
throughout this puzzle T stands for a tree; the may is the hawthorn

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled to hear that a certain letter is hell.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle the letter T stands in for the name of a tree, here MAY, the hawthorn; 'is' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of alarm and distress, a synonym of consternation.

clue.text: Low joint in which the S-Sun will lose its identity

indicators.note: the second part goes inside the low joint

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club
S followed by sol, the Latin word for sun

explanation.surface: In a seedy club, the sun will fade away to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve is to melt away into something else, no longer remaining distinct.

clue.text: Out, as everyone can see

explanation.surface: Someone is out, which is obvious to all.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking workers are out on strike; something striking is conspicuous, plain for all to notice.

clue.text: Revert to original speed to promote team operation

indicators.note: promoting letters moves them up to new places, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone wants to go back to the old pace to encourage teamwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote' raises the A of TEAM and the P of OP, giving ATEM and PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempo is the musical instruction to resume the original pace after a change.

clue.text: T for the old old story

explanation.surface: A letter is said to be the same old tale.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for a tree throughout; the horse or sweet chestnut is one, and a chestnut is also a joke or tale heard too often.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the chestnut tree; the second is the idiom for a stale, much-repeated anecdote.

clue.text: HT for steerage?

parts.note: the first of the two letters printed, H, is taken as written
the second printed letter is T, which stands for a tree throughout this puzzle; here the elm

explanation.surface: A couple of letters stand for the steering gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is a ship's wheel or tiller, the means of steering.

clue.text: Ashamed to be in wolf's clothing?

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed to be dressed like a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition inverts the wolf in sheep's clothing: a creature like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish means embarrassed; read as sheep-ish it also means like a sheep.

clue.text: How much to prevent feeling?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what it costs to stop sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: A number answers the question of quantity; a numbing agent, something more numb, deadens sensation.

clue.text: During starter old railwaymen find occupation

indicators.note: the railwaymen come during, so within, the starter

parts.note: a golf hole starts from the tee
NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, now merged

explanation.surface: Railway staff find work during the opening course of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course but is the tee where a golf hole starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding or occupation of a post or property.

clue.text: T in a little way or a long way

indicators.note: the tree is placed inside the short form for a road

parts.note: ST is the short form of ..., a little way written small
T stands for a tree throughout this puzzle, and here it is simply the word tree itself

explanation.surface: A letter sits inside a short road, or a long one.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the theme letter gives the word TREE itself, put inside ST. 'A little way' (an abbreviated way) contrasts with 'a long way', the full word.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, a way through a town, written out at full length.

clue.text: T on island in local government

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another comes before it

parts.note: T stands for a tree throughout this puzzle; the alder grows by water
the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A letter on an island turns out to sit on the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: An alderman is a senior member of a British borough or city council.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is an elected councillor, someone serving in a town or city council.

clue.text: Not a serious writer-that may bold the baby

parts.note: play is what is done in fun, not seriously
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A comic author might be left holding the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a portable enclosure where an infant is kept safely.

clue.text: Enough gall for two Ts

parts.note: T stands for a tree throughout this puzzle; the first of the two trees is the oak
the second tree is the apple

explanation.surface: Someone has the cheek to claim two letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gall' looks like cheek, as in 'enough gall', but it is the growth on a tree; the answer's name is made of two tree names.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a round swelling caused on oak twigs by a wasp, a kind of plant gall.

clue.text: Look like a quiet T

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
T stands for a tree throughout this puzzle; here the pear tree

explanation.surface: Something seems to resemble a hushed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to seem, as in 'it looks like rain'.

clue.text: Migrant to get liquid refreshment

explanation.surface: A traveller stops to have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a migratory bird; to swallow is to gulp down a drink.

clue.text: T like god when princess has gone

indicators.note: when the princess has gone she is no longer there, so her letters are taken away

parts.note: divine means godlike
Di, Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A letter resembles a god once a princess has left.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for a tree or plant throughout; the grapevine is the tree-like climber meant.
explanation.definitionFit: In this puzzle T means a tree, and the vine is a woody climbing plant grown for grapes.

clue.text: English pair of Ts? Nonsense!

parts.note: T stands for a tree throughout this puzzle; the first tree is the yew
the second tree is the ash

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a pair of English letters as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is talk meant to deceive, humbug or rubbish.

clue.text: Music player, the best, absorbs shocking ment by right

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'shocking ment', a garbled OCR of 'shocking treatment' (ECT); restoring it needs more than three letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Music player, the best, absorbs shocking ment by right

clue.text: Person in ring to study gold

parts.note: to read is to study, as at university
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring wants to study gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, who performs in the bullring.

clue.text: Marine batting, entering duck at the end of the line

definitions.text: at the end of the line

indicators.note: the marine and batting pieces go into the duck

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
RM is the Royal Marines
a batsman in cricket is in

explanation.surface: A marine at the crease goes in for a duck at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is also a score of nought in cricket, which suits 'batting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the station or stop where a route finishes.

clue.text: T left on your head? Getting on!

parts.note: T stands for a tree throughout this puzzle; here the elder

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A letter left on someone's head is a sign of advancing years.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on is ageing, past middle age.

clue.text: T (name immaterial?) removed from bed

explanation.surface: A letter is taken out of a garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition alludes to Juliet's line that the flower would smell as sweet by any other name; the second is 'got up from bed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the shrub of Shakespeare's famous line; the second is the past tense of getting up.

clue.text: Giving of cash seen as afterthought in the Bible

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added as an afterthought
alms are money given to the poor

explanation.surface: A gift of money is mentioned as an afterthought in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms are a book of sacred songs in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Language of painter about a year before Christ

annotationWithheld.why: Language of painter about a year before Christ: ARABIC = ARA + B(I)C needs I, which 'a year' does not give; probably a misread word
annotationWithheld.clue: Language of painter about a year before Christ

clue.text: Part for one that sang in America is bad for the heart

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A singer's role in America is unhealthy for the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle.

clue.text: T for tidy

explanation.surface: A letter stands for neatness.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the evergreen conifer; the second means smart and neat in appearance.

clue.text: T has a hooter on the side

indicators.note: one piece placed on another comes before it in an across clue

parts.note: a horn is a hooter, as on a car
a ship's beam is its side, as in 'on the beam'

explanation.surface: A letter carries a horn mounted on its side.
explanation.definitionFit: T means a tree in this puzzle, and the hornbeam is a hardwood tree used for hedging.

clue.text: Raised up by rights, as Moggy said

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upwards, reading from the bottom

parts.note: R is right, so two rights give RR

explanation.surface: A cat stands on its hind legs, as the pet itself said.
explanation.walkthrough: Moggy is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A purr is the contented sound a cat makes, its way of speaking.

clue.text: American city to set fire hesitantly to T

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to burn is to set fire to something
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An arsonist from Los Angeles dithers about setting light to a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: T means a tree in this puzzle, and the laburnum is a small tree with yellow hanging flowers.

clue.text: T rescues man from Cherwell

indicators.note: to rescue the man is to take him out of the name, removing those letters

parts.note: Frederick Lindemann, Churchill's scientific adviser, became Viscount Cherwell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A letter saves a person from the Oxford river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cherwell is a river in Oxford, but here it is the peer's title, standing for Lord Cherwell's surname, Lindemann.
explanation.definitionFit: T means a tree in this puzzle, and the linden is another name for the lime tree.

clue.text: T, a servant in the days of the Raj, keeping the Latins' love

indicators.note: one word holding another keeps it inside

parts.words: a servant in the days of the Raj
parts.note: a syce was a groom employed in British India
amor is Latin for love

explanation.surface: A letter, a colonial servant, clings to the Romans' love.
explanation.walkthrough: The Raj was British rule in India.
explanation.definitionFit: T means a tree in this puzzle, and the sycamore is a large maple tree.

clue.text: T catching the audience's eye on a rock in the Rhine

indicators.note: the tree that has caught an eye onto itself makes the rock's name, so the eye is taken off again
an audience hears the name, so it is a matter of sound

parts.note: the Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine where a siren lured boatmen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A letter attracts attention at a famous rock on the German river.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the rock's name sounds like the tree with 'eye' on the end; 'catching ... eye on' says the eye is added to the tree, so removing it from the sound leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: T means a tree in this puzzle, and the laurel is the bay tree whose leaves crowned victors.
